idiom_name: HttpClient + StandardResilienceHandler (Polly) with an explicit Idempotency-Key
implementation_notes: The retry half is library work: Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience's standard handler stacks rate limiter, total timeout, retry, circuit breaker and attempt timeout around IHttpClientFactory-created HttpClients, so a hand-written retry loop is no longer justified. What the library deliberately does not do is make the call idempotent - it retries POST, PATCH, PUT and DELETE like any other method unless told otherwise - so for non-replayable calls you either use options.Retry.DisableForUnsafeHttpMethods()/DisableFor(...) or mint an Idempotency-Key (Guid.NewGuid() captured above the pipeline) and let the endpoint deduplicate. The key belongs to the logical operation, not to a DelegatingHandler, and a replay returns the server's recorded outcome.
pitfalls: The standard resilience handler retries all HTTP methods by default; a POST that creates a record is duplicated unless the endpoint is keyed or the strategy is restricted with DisableFor/DisableForUnsafeHttpMethods.
The same HttpRequestMessage must be replayed: building the message (and therefore the header) inside the pipeline or a custom handler mints a new key per attempt.
AddStandardHedgingHandler sends concurrent attempts by design, so it is only safe for naturally idempotent operations - a key does not make parallel duplicates harmless.
